what_its_for: Pilocarpine is used for two main purposes depending on its form. The eye drop form helps lower pressure inside your eye and is used to treat glaucoma and certain eye conditions. The pill form helps increase saliva production in people who have dry mouth caused by radiation treatment for head and neck cancer, or from a condition called Sjogren's syndrome.
how_to_take: FOR EYE DROPS: Wash your hands before and after using. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to make a small pocket, and place the prescribed number of drops into that pocket. Gently close your eye for 1 to 2 minutes. Press your finger lightly against the inner corner of your eye to stop the medicine from draining. Avoid touching the dropper tip to your eye or any surface. If using more than one eye medicine, wait at least 5 minutes between each one. FOR TABLETS: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You may take it with food if it upsets your stomach.
dosing: FOR EYE DROPS: The usual dose is 1 to 2 drops placed in the affected eye up to 4 times a day, or as directed by your doctor. FOR TABLETS: The usual starting dose is 5 mg taken 3 times a day with meals. Your doctor may increase your dose up to 10 mg three times a day based on how well it works for you and how well you tolerate it. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not take more or less than directed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it or use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or use extra doses to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store pilocarpine tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Store eye drops as directed on the label, usually at room temperature. Some eye drops may need to be refrigerated, so always check the package instructions. Keep all forms of this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery right after using pilocarpine eye drops, as they may cause blurry vision or make it harder to see in dim or dark conditions, especially at night. Avoid activities that require sharp, clear vision until you know how the medicine affects you. If you take the tablet form, avoid becoming overheated or dehydrated, as pilocarpine can cause excessive sweating. Limit alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can worsen side effects like dizziness. Tell your doctor before taking any other eye drops or medicines, including over-the-counter products.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: sudden or severe vision changes, eye pain or redness that gets worse, chest pain or a fast or irregular heartbeat, difficulty breathing or wheezing, severe sweating, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that does not go away, dizziness or fainting, confusion or unusual changes in mood, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or severe headache. Also call your doctor if your dry mouth or eye pressure does not seem to be improving after a few weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: FOR EYE DROPS: Pilocarpine eye drops usually start working within 10 to 30 minutes of putting them in your eye and the effects may last 4 to 8 hours. FOR TABLETS: If you are taking pilocarpine tablets for dry mouth, you may start to notice more saliva production within 1 hour of taking your dose. The full benefit may take several weeks of regular use to notice. Keep taking your medicine as prescribed even if you do not feel immediate improvement.
special_populations: PREGNANCY AND BREASTFEEDING: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of pilocarpine during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established, so your doctor will weigh the benefits and risks before prescribing it. OLDER ADULTS: Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of pilocarpine, especially dizziness and sweating. Use extra caution to avoid falls. KIDNEY OR LIVER PROBLEMS: If you have kidney or liver disease, your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely. CHILDREN: Pilocarpine tablets are generally not recommended for children. Eye drop use in children should be supervised by a doctor.
